name: He 178 gas-turbine jet flight
description: A Heinkel He 178 aircraft flew under gas-turbine jet propulsion in 1939, combining von Ohain’s engine development with an aircraft.

date.basis: The cited account dates this scoped episode.

events.statement: The Heinkel He 178 flew with a gas-turbine jet engine developed by Hans von Ohain with Heinkel. NASA identifies Erich Warsitz as pilot.
events.caveats: British and German turbojet development proceeded in parallel; this flight does not settle priority of all jet concepts.

evidence.supports: NASA history describes the flight, aircraft and developer.

evidence.locator: Book announcements, The First Jet Pilot
evidence.supports: Names Warsitz and dates He 178 flight.

contributions.resource: Developed the gas-turbine engine with Heinkel

evidence.supports: NASA says von Ohain collaborated with Heinkel to build the engine flown on He 178.

contributions.resource: Collaborated on development of the engine flown on He 178

evidence.supports: NASA identifies the Heinkel Company as von Ohain’s engine-development collaborator.

evidence.locator: Book announcements, The First Jet Pilot
evidence.supports: NASA newsletter identifies Warsitz as the pilot of the 27 August 1939 flight.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established for this scoped record in the inspected sources, not a certified global priority.

caveats: This experimental flight does not imply commercial passenger service or a sole inventor of jet propulsion.

research.note: Second-reader check of named facets against NASA history and newsletter book description; airline use and a complete account of aircraft design are outside these sources.

people.note: Developed the engine in collaboration with Heinkel; this does not attribute the entire aircraft to him.

places.note: Country-level reference; event narrative gives the more specific location where established.
